_README: Triaged credential findings in this repository's GIT HISTORY. Scanned by
`node scripts/check-secrets.js --history`, which is part of preflight.
History cannot be cleaned without a rewrite, so the gate is each finding's STATUS, not its
rotate-required : the credential is exposed and may still be valid. FAILS once
accepted_until has passed. Rotate it, then set status to retired.
retired         : rotated out of use. Passes, and if watch_sha12 is present the value is
placeholder     : triaged as never having been a credential.
NEVER add a hash of a LIVE secret to this file. It lives in a PUBLIC repository, and a hash
of a weak secret is a brute-force target. Only a value that is already compromised AND
rotated out of use may carry a watch_sha12 -- at which point the hash protects nothing that
still matters. A finding that is exposed but not yet rotated is recorded WITHOUT a hash of
its value, which is why the admin-password entry below has none.

conclusion: Exactly one real credential is in this repository's history: the production admin
password. Because the repository is public, it has been readable by anyone on the internet
since 2026-10-27, and removing it from the tip the same day did not remove it from history.
Measured NOT to be in history: the GitHub personal access token, the Railway Postgres
password, and the three webhook/trigger secrets -- 0 commits each. No .env was ever
committed; only .env.example, with placeholder values. No vendor-prefixed API key
(Anthropic, OpenAI, Resend, AWS, Google, Twilio, Slack, SendGrid, Stripe) appears in any
Those credentials are exposed through the project handoff document instead, which is a
different and smaller blast radius: everyone with access to that document, plus anyone it
was pasted to. They still require rotation; they do not require assuming the whole internet

findings.removed_from_tip: 98a0765 on 2026-10-27 -- 'Day 0: stop committing credentials, and make rotation provable'
findings.exposure: PUBLIC git history of a public repository, since 2026-10-27. Not recoverable by deletion.
note: No hash of this value is stored, because it may still be live and this file is public.
Once the password is changed, set status to 'retired' and add watch_sha12 of the OLD
value so its reappearance is caught; at that point the hash is harmless.
accepted_until is deliberately 7 days, not the 90 granted to the AWS credential
exception in ruling 18 item 3. A publicly exposed admin password does not get a quarter.
Past that date this check fails and preflight goes red, which is the intended behaviour:
shipping more code matters less than an exposed production login.
Production login has been returning password_mismatch since 2026-11-06, which may mean
the password was already changed. 'May' is not a remediation record, so this stays
rotate-required until the change is confirmed.
